questions.q: In Scenario 1, Harbor Point Logistics' invoice is stuck unvalidated. What is the actual cause?
options: A pricing error on the invoice
A Quantity Received hold, because only part of the PO quantity has been received
The supplier's bank account is invalid
The invoice was never matched to a purchase order
questions.explain: Only 180 of 200 pallets had been received, triggering a Quantity Received hold under three-way matching.

questions.q: In Scenario 2, Cascade Industrial Parts says they were never paid even though Payables shows the invoice as paid. What should be checked first?
options: Whether the payment file was actually transmitted to and received by the bank
Whether the supplier's address is correctly formatted
Whether a new purchase order needs to be created
Whether the invoice needs to be re-validated
questions.explain: A payment showing as issued in Oracle but never reaching the bank points to a transmission failure, which calls for void-and-reissue, not a brand-new invoice.

questions.q: In Scenario 3, Solace Robotics has a $2,400 gap on its Payables-to-Ledger Reconciliation report. How should this be diagnosed?
options: By re-entering every invoice from scratch
By assuming it is always a currency conversion error
By tracing the gap through the accounted, transferred, and posted stages
By ignoring it since small differences are expected
questions.explain: Reconciliation gaps are diagnosed by checking which of the three pipeline stages (accounted/transferred/posted) a transaction got stuck at.

questions.q: In Scenario 4, what does Meridian Office Supply's growing accrual balance most likely require?
options: No action -- accrual balances always grow over time
Switching Meridian to two-way matching
Cancelling all of Meridian's purchase orders
Separating normal timing gaps from stale, uncorrected balances, and manually correcting the stale portion
questions.explain: The Accrual Reconciliation Report distinguishes expected timing gaps from stale balances tied to cancelled POs, which need a manual correcting entry.

questions.q: What course comes next after completing Oracle Fusion Accounts Payable, according to the Financials Configuration stage of the Oracle Fusion Financials Consultant path?
options: Cash Management
Accounts Receivable
Fixed Assets
General Ledger
questions.explain: Accounts Receivable follows Accounts Payable in the Financials Configuration stage, covering the customer side of the same kind of transactions.
